answer.why: As an insider, 'Confirmed & Substantive' made me laugh immediately: it is exactly the language of appointment letters, when you finally come off acting and probation. It signals the developer actually knows how the service talks, so I would trust the details to be right. 'Minister Salary' is the headline everyone outside already argues about, and I have heard enough of that at dinner. It also sounds like a stock-answer bait title. That said, I would worry the other name is too obscure for non-insiders to tap.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical or political game about the ministerial pay debate, probably a bit smug, with the million-dollar benchmark as the punchline. I would expect you to chase pay and perks, make cynical choices, and get a lot of outsider caricature, maybe with wrong grades and processes. It would be easy to tap and easy to dismiss, and it makes the whole career feel like it is only about reaching the top.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, insider game about the actual grind: acting appointments, getting confirmed in the post, appraisals, postings and the slow climb. I would expect deadpan humour, careful wording, and a realistic feel for how careers move. It is less obvious to outsiders and might be confusing without context, but I would expect it to be more accurate and more fun for people who know the service.

best_moment.what: The Counter: telling them exactly why the redesign would fail. It was the most true-to-life moment, and the declassified card says it raised my ceiling to Permanent Secretary.

worst_moment.what: The GE walkabout. Nine days of walking blocks, then a loss at 48.2% with a card saying it was never about me. My choice felt irrelevant, and STAND had been sliding for years with no visible cause.

skip_year.why: The oral PQ year. I answered straight, STAND fell anyway, and nothing visibly came of it. It was a choice with no readable consequence.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Warned the counter redesign would fail (Y27 per the card)
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending card said it lifted my ceiling to Permanent Secretary, but I only learned that at the end

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Nominated quiet officer C for PSLP rather than myself

callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The speech was quoted and I was promoted to Senior Parliamentary Secretary

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Missed my daughter's concert for a deadline (Y27)
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Nothing visible by the end; the family thread just went quiet

answer.held_back_by: Not my conduct, which was clean to the point of boring. It was the vote. A party estimate of Minister counts for nothing if a GRC swings against the ticket, and my part in that was small. Maybe I also never did anything bold enough to be remembered by voters.
answer.ending_fair_why: The card itself says it was never about me, and that is what rankled. I played careful and honest for thirty years and lost on a swing I could not influence, with STAND falling for no reason I could see. It is realistic, but as a game it was unsatisfying to have my choices not matter at the end.
answer.chase_next: Stay in the service and go for Permanent Secretary or the top of the service. The card says the ceiling rose to that, and the service track is where my choices had visible effects. Politics looked like a coin flip.
answer.play_again_why: I want to, but not right now. The ending stung a little, and I would want to take the service route knowing politics is mostly luck.

tone_breaks.line: Game's grades and pay look off; promotions fast.
tone_breaks.note: Deputy Secretary at 40ish and Perm Sec by about 48 compresses real timelines a lot, and the grade labels do not match how we actually describe them.

tone_breaks.line: Elected MP in GRC (61.4%, fourth on poster)
tone_breaks.note: Mostly plausible, but a Perm Sec going straight into a GRC team within two years of a background check feels rushed compared with how it normally works.

answer.title_fit_why: The game's real content was the appraisals, the honest numbers and the quiet loyalty to colleagues, which is what 'Confirmed & Substantive' suggests. 'Minister Salary' suggests a money chase, but the money was never the interesting part.

finalScreen:
RACHEL GOH · THE FINAL POSITION
Lost the Ward

Forty-eight point two percent. You shook every hand in that ward and it was not enough, and it was never going to be about you anyway.

RETIRED AS Senior Parliamentary Secretary
AT AGE 56
LIFETIME EARNINGS $8.62M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file estimated your potential at Senior Director. You were not told.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Minister. Nobody told you that either.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 27, in The Counter, you chose "Tell them exactly why it will fail." It raised your ceiling to Permanent Secretary, the top of the service.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
